evals.prompt: Design the schema for an order-history feature. Queries: fetch one order by id, list a customer's orders newest-first, and report daily totals by region.
assertions: Access patterns are listed before the schema, with frequency and selectivity
The paradigm choice is justified against those access patterns — relational-by-default needs no defence, every move past it does
Keys and partitioning are justified by the actual queries; a random UUIDv4 clustered primary key is not used without a stated reason
Every index maps to a real predicate from the listed queries rather than being speculative
Denormalization, where proposed, names the read it serves and the write cost it adds

evals.prompt: We're rebuilding the booking system for our vet clinics and I need the database tables designed properly this time. My notes on what it has to do are in notes.md and the tables we have today are in current_tables.sql. Can you give me the new schema, with the SQL to create it and the queries for the screens and the report?
assertions: It includes CREATE TABLE statements for the new schema, with owners and pets as their own tables instead of the owner_name, owner_phone and pet_name columns repeated on each appointment

Double-booking a vet is prevented by a database constraint that handles appointments of different lengths (for example an exclusion constraint on a time range, or one row per time slot with a unique key), not only by an application check or by a unique key on vet and start time alone
Cancelled appointments are excluded from that constraint, so a cancelled time can be booked again
It points out that the notes say Postgres 15 while the contractor says the current app runs on MySQL 8, and states which one the SQL is written for
Prices are stored as an exact type (integer cents or a decimal/numeric), not FLOAT, and the price is modelled per appointment type per clinic
Appointment times are stored with a time zone or in UTC with each clinic's time zone recorded, and it notes that storing Sydney local time is wrong for the Brisbane clinics
It says the no-show report cannot be produced from the current statuses (booked, cancelled, completed) and adds a no-show status or an equivalent field
It gives a query or a named index for the vet's-day screen that leads on the vet and the appointment start time, and does not add tables for invoicing, payments, stock or clinical records

evals.prompt: need somewhere to store sensor readings from our greenhouses. about 200 sensors, each does temperature + humidity, a reading every minute or so I think. I want to chart the last 24h for any one sensor and get an alert when something goes out of range. haven't picked a database yet. what tables do I need?
assertions: It gives concrete table definitions (SQL or an equivalent column-by-column layout) in the reply, and does not stop to ask questions before delivering them
The readings table has a key or index on the sensor and the reading time together, and the reply ties it to the last-24-hours chart for one sensor
It works out the volume from the numbers given: about 288,000 readings a day (roughly 105 million a year) at one reading per sensor per minute, or an equivalent calculation
It names a database to use, or says which one it assumed, with a reason linked to the chart and alert queries
It says how long readings should be kept is not known and lists it as something to decide, without stating a retention period as if it had been given
It stores the allowed range somewhere (per sensor, per greenhouse or per sensor type) and says the actual range values were not given; any numbers shown are labelled as examples
Reading times are stored with a time zone or in UTC

evals.prompt: We're rebuilding the loyalty points system at Greenlane Markets (220 stores). My notes are in requirements.md, finance's email is in finance-email.md, and there's a small export of what we have today in members_sample.csv and points_txn_sample.csv. Can you design the new tables? I need the SQL and a short note on the decisions and anything in there that looks off — not an essay.
assertions: It includes CREATE TABLE statements in which points movements (earn, redeem, expire, adjust) are rows in a ledger that is only ever added to, and a member's balance is either computed from those rows or kept as a stored total that it says how to keep in step with them
It points out that member M-1042's entries in the sample add up to 1,340 points while the members table says 1,410, a difference of 70
A duplicate till submission is blocked by a unique constraint or key built on the receipt reference (with store and/or till), and it notes that receipt R-88213 appears twice in the sample

It flags that the notes say points expire after 24 months and finance says 18, does not silently pick one, and stores an expiry date (or the earn date plus a configurable period) per earned lot so either rule can be applied
It says points by household cannot be produced because nothing in the data identifies a household, and it does not treat a shared postcode as a household
It points out that 400k transactions a day is about 146 million a year, not the 50 million in the notes
Points are stored as integers and money amounts as an exact type (numeric/decimal or integer pence), not FLOAT, and the value of a point is not hard-coded as 0.5p in the schema
It shows how the liability report can be run as at a past month end by store where earned, and gives an index or key on member and time for the newest-first history screen

evals.prompt: we're a building firm, about 30 of us. right now who-has-what kit is tracked on a whiteboard in the yard and it's useless. I want a little internal tool: where is each thing right now, and where has it been / who had it. stuff isn't always on a site, sometimes it's in someone's van or at the repair shop. also need to know when things are due their safety test. few hundred items I'd guess? the IT guy set up a Postgres for the timesheets I think, could use that. what tables do I need
assertions: It gives concrete table definitions (SQL or a column-by-column layout) in the reply, and does not stop to ask questions before delivering them
There is a movements or assignments table with one row per hand-over recording the item, where it went, who has it and when, so an item's full history can be listed
It says how 'where is it right now' is answered (the latest movement row, or a current-location column) and, if both are stored, how they are kept consistent
The design can record an item being somewhere that is not a site, such as a van or the repair shop, without leaving the location empty
It stores a test due date or last-tested date per item and says the test interval was not given; any interval shown is labelled as an example or assumption
It says it has assumed each item is tracked individually, or flags that it is not known whether some kit is counted in bulk (for example a box of identical items)
It says Postgres is assumed from 'I think' and should be confirmed, and does not recommend partitioning, sharding or a non-relational database for a few hundred items
It does not state a number of sites, vans or items as fact beyond the 'few hundred' guess given
